investigation.trigger: How does X work. Why was Y built this way. Are we sure about Z.
investigation.gives: A cited answer in how-shaped sections. No code changes.
investigation.note: Read-only. The throughput checkpoint is explicitly n/a, so it will not pad the answer with work you did not ask for.

bug-fix.trigger: A defect to reproduce and fix. 'Repro first, then fix and verify.'
bug-fix.gives: A root-caused fix with runtime evidence, commits staged so the failing repro lands before the fix.
bug-fix.note: Step 1 makes the agent reproduce it itself on the real surface. It will not hand the repro back to you except under one narrow stated exception.

perf-issue.gives: A traced fix compared against a baseline, with the measurement cited in the PR.
perf-issue.note: It captures the baseline before hypothesising. A perf claim without a trace does not pass.

hillclimb.trigger: Move one metric to a target over many attempts.
hillclimb.gives: One commit per accepted win, a decision log of every hypothesis, before and after.
hillclimb.note: Distinct from perf-issue, which is a one-off fix. Here a plateau is not a stop: it pivots category and keeps going.

runtime-forensics.trigger: A live symptom: a leak, idle CPU spin, a visual glitch.
runtime-forensics.gives: A diagnosis mapped to file, symbol and line. Not a fix.
runtime-forensics.note: It proves the mechanism by instrumenting the running process before believing it.

trace-forensics.trigger: A captured artifact handed to you: cpuprofile, trace, spindump, heap snapshot.
trace-forensics.gives: A cited diagnosis, no fix unless you ask.
trace-forensics.note: It loads the artifact into something queryable rather than eyeballing it, and routes onward to bug-fix or perf-issue once the cause is known.

feature.gives: A feature built from a named data shape, verified on the real surface, in small ordered commits.
feature.note: Step 1 is `/how` over the affected subsystem and step 2 is `/architect`. Skipping either is recorded, not silent.

refactoring.trigger: Change the shape without changing behaviour.
refactoring.gives: A behaviour-preserving reshape, proven unchanged on the real artifact.
refactoring.note: It pins the behaviour contract first and subtracts before it adds. 'It compiles' is not the proof.

prototype.trigger: Settle a design or behavioural question cheaply. 'Mock it up', 'try this layout'.
prototype.gives: The decision, plus throwaway code you are meant to discard.
prototype.note: This is how pstack answers questions you might otherwise be asked. If observation can settle it, it builds rather than asks.

visual-parity.trigger: Pixel-exact equivalence between two implementations, or a styling migration.
visual-parity.gives: Component-by-component parity verified by image diff.
visual-parity.note: It establishes the baseline harness before migrating, and holds explicit anti-shortcut clauses: no harness edits, no baseline tampering.

authoring-a-skill.gives: A validated skill with resolving links, plus a PR.
authoring-a-skill.note: Agent-facing prose has a higher bar than human prose: an unhelpful sentence becomes an instruction some future agent follows.

eval.trigger: Does this skill or prompt change actually improve behaviour.
eval.gives: A blinded verdict from parallel candidates and a judge on a different model family.
eval.note: It grades from the transcripts, not from what the candidates claim they did.

babysit.trigger: 'Check on PR X', 'get it green', 'address the review comments'.
babysit.gives: A PR or stack driven to merge-ready.
babysit.note: Works the merge frontier only, never mutates stack topology, and orders work conflicts then review threads then CI.

shipping.gives: The contiguous verified run landed bottom-up.
shipping.note: Green is not safe. Nothing lands without an independent per-PR verdict from an agent that did not write the code.

opening-a-pr.trigger: Automatic. Runs at the end of every playbook that ships a code change.
opening-a-pr.gives: A ready PR: small ordered commits, conventional title, briefing-style body.
opening-a-pr.note: You will rarely invoke this yourself.

autonomous-run.trigger: 'Run until done', 'don't stop', 'I'm going to bed'.
autonomous-run.gives: A long task driven to a predicate you can check, with a decision log.
autonomous-run.note: State the exit condition as something checkable before it starts. A vague finish condition is the one thing this playbook cannot work with.

orchestrate.trigger: 'Own this migration until it lands.' Multi-day, many stacked PRs.
orchestrate.gives: A standing program under one coordinator, with a ledger and a rolling window of workers.
orchestrate.note: Heavier than autonomous-run. Work one agent could finish in a session belongs there, however program-shaped it sounds.

autopilot-full.trigger: 'Autopilot this queue.' Independent PRs, run to merged.
autopilot-full.gives: One owner per PR carrying build through merge, each head verified at the root before it lands.
autopilot-full.note: Grants merge authority. The irreversible-action guard still applies: no deploys, no data deletion, no customer messages.

autopilot-stack.gives: One linear verified base-branch stack for you to review and merge.
autopilot-stack.note: Same loop as autopilot-full minus the merge. No owner merges or arms auto-merge.

multi-phase-plan.trigger: Work spanning phases or stacked PRs.
multi-phase-plan.gives: A written plan validated by a script, then executed.
multi-phase-plan.note: If the change is one or two files with an obvious approach it says so and stops rather than producing a plan you do not need.

session-pickup.trigger: Resuming or taking over in-flight work.
session-pickup.gives: Reconstructed state, a done-vs-pending diff, and a route to the right playbook.
session-pickup.note: It verifies the inherited claims against the real artifact rather than trusting the previous agent's summary.

pause-safely.trigger: Going offline, restarting, or about to lose context.
pause-safely.gives: Durable work and a resume note.
pause-safely.note: It stops at a safe boundary and takes no irreversible action to pause. The complement to session-pickup.

worktree-cleanup.note: Untracked work is never dropped unattended: never-committed files exist nowhere else, so it shows you the list and waits.
